### How this work is cited

Passages inside Letters to Lucilius are identified by epistle and section (e.g. ep. 104.26). Several letters quote an earlier author — Cleanthes, Hecato, Epicurus — and in those the quoted sentence is that author's, delivered in Seneca's Latin. The archive records the inner attribution in the source field where it is known.

### The work in Seneca’s thought

Lucius Annaeus Seneca (c. 4 BCE–65 CE) was a Cordoban-born Stoic, tragic playwright, and adviser—later forced suicide victim—under Nero. [More on Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) .
